0. Getting started

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-00-start.Rmd
book-00-start.Rmd

What you will learn

Install the client packages, connect to the Opal server and choose a resource.

Before you start

The book uses an Opal server at https://localhost:8443. Its administrator has already loaded the data as OMOP CDM resources and installed dsOMOP and dsBase on its R server. You work only on the client side: you send requests and receive aggregate results, never patient rows. The data are synthetic, so the results teach methods; they are not clinical findings.

You need R 4.1 or newer. Install the client packages once:

install.packages(c("remotes", "DSI", "DSOpal"))
remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBaseClient@6.3.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("isglobal-brge/dsOMOPClient@2.10.5", upgrade = "never")

Connect to the Opal server

ds.omop.login() logs in to the server and attaches one OMOP CDM resource:

library(dsOMOPClient)
conns <- ds.omop.login("https://localhost:8443", user = "administrator",
  password = "password", resource = "omop.gibleed", server = "site")$conns

Use the user name and password your administrator gave you, and keep them out of shared scripts; with a personal access token, pass token = "<token>" instead. omop.gibleed is the resource: project omop, resource gibleed. site is the name this book gives the connection. conns holds the connection, not patient rows; every later call sends its request through it.

Check the client and the server 

ds.omop.client.version()
#> [1] "2.10.5"
ds.omop.server.version(conns = conns)[c("server", "published", "running", "ready")]
server published running ready
site 2.10.5 2.10.5 TRUE

The first line is the client package on your computer. ready confirms that the server’s installed dsOMOP and its available methods agree.

The resources on the server

Each chapter names the resource it uses. All of them are in the project omop:

Resource Contents
omop.gibleed GiBleed: 2,694 synthetic people with visits, conditions and medicines; no numeric lab values
omop.synthea Synthea27Nj: 28 synthetic people with numeric lab values and units
omop.questionnaire A synthetic questionnaire study of 48 people, described below
omop.questionnaire_vocab The questionnaire with a richer teaching vocabulary: codes, synonyms and hierarchies
omop.questionnaire_drugs The questionnaire vocabulary plus medicine supply histories
omop.questionnaire_formulas The questionnaire plus serum creatinine and repeated same-day weights
omop.questionnaire_site2 A second site’s questionnaire, with different answers and wording
omop.synthea_north, omop.synthea_south Synthea27Nj split into two sites with different people
omop.gibleed_north, omop.gibleed_south GiBleed split into two sites with different people

GiBleed and Synthea27Nj are the public OHDSI Eunomia datasets. Analyst results report counts in five-person bands, so you will see 2,690 rather than 2,694.

The questionnaire study has four groups of twelve people. Two groups answer the education question twice, swapping Secondary and University between their first and last answers; they also answer a yes/no fever question. One group has only a birth year; one has neither visits nor a death record. Knowing this design lets you predict the results of later chapters:

Item Total Female Male
People 48 20 28
Education respondents 24 10 14
Education answer rows 48 20 28
Fever answer rows 24 10 14
Inpatient visits 24 10 14
Outpatient visits 36 14 22
2023: myocardial infarction 12 4 8
2023: pneumonia 6 3 3
2024: myocardial infarction 12 4 8
2024: pneumonia 6 3 3
Survivors 12 6 6

There are 24 education respondents but 48 education answer rows: an answer row is not a person.

Exercise 1: choose the lab resource

Attach omop.synthea instead of GiBleed and request its person count. How can you tell that you are no longer querying GiBleed?

Solution

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
ds.omop.connect(resource = "omop.synthea", conns = conns)
ds.omop.table.stats("person", conns = conns)
#> <dsomop_result>
#> Servers: site
#> Scope: per_site
#>
#> $site
#> $rows
#> [1] 25
#>
#> $persons
#> [1] 25

The person count is 25, meaning 25–29 people. That band contains Synthea27Nj’s 28 people and is far below GiBleed’s 2,694. Chapter 1 explains these bands. ds.omop.disconnect() releases the attached resource; the login stays open.

Exercise 2: log in again

End the session, then log in again with GiBleed. Confirm the database with a person count, rather than checking only that a connection has a name.

Solution

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
DSI::datashield.logout(conns)
conns <- ds.omop.login("https://localhost:8443", user = "administrator",
  password = "password", resource = "omop.gibleed", server = "site")$conns
ds.omop.table.stats("person", conns = conns)
#> <dsomop_result>
#> Servers: site
#> Scope: per_site
#>
#> $site
#> $rows
#> [1] 2690
#>
#> $persons
#> [1] 2690

The count is back to the 2,690–2,694 band. Disconnect releases the resource; logout closes the DataSHIELD session. A new login starts a new session.

Recap

The client packages are installed, ds.omop.login() opens a resource on the server, and conns carries your requests.
